title: Voice studio controls
summary: The voice actuator: start or stop the speech service, say something in a chosen voice, read a file back as text - and record every clip by the bytes really written.

surfaces.usb: DEGRADED(promotion pending - authored and certified on PC first, then carried to the stick per-file and hash-verified, where the stick runs its own suite)
surfaces.web: N/A(by steward decision 2026-09-26: a browser tab has no local VoiceStudio install to bridge to, so a card there could only offer a button that cannot work)

notes: The actuator half of the voice pair: lygo.voiceinfo reads the facts and this module is where a voice is actually ASKED FOR. It says nothing itself - every clip leaves through the voice_harness machinery, which is the one place that knows how to call the separate application, and comes back with a receipt naming the absolute path, byte count and sha256 read BACK off the disk, because claimed and written must be the same thing. It owns exactly one thing - save/voice, the operator's engine and voice choice plus one record per clip - written through atomicio behind the p0 gate, and the text to be spoken is gated before anything is sent. It never writes into VoiceStudio's own folders. `stop` refuses by name to kill a backend this console did not start: a service started by VoiceStudio's own window belongs to the operator, and taking it down would take their application with it.
